transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-09-08
Start: 16:30 PT — Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Ortiz (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (Deckhand Lead Eng), Ethan Brooks (Deckhand CTO), Marta Diaz (Deckhand DevOps)

Summary:
Quick orientation for Deckhand Labs engineering team to get Redwood SDKs running in Python and TypeScript, cover API keys/SSO options, sandbox env, and next steps for a short POC. Demo shows local quickstart, env var pattern for CI, and pointers for private/VPC options. Some latency/cost tradeoffs discussed, plus request for SOC2 and deployment docs.

Topics:
- Quickstart repo and local run through (py + ts)
- Auth patterns: api key vs SSO + service accounts + rotation
- Sandbox env setup: tokens, .env, secrets in CI, k8s secret patterns
- Optimize tips: batching, prefix caching, model selection
- Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC

Action items (as noted): see metadata above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh we have about an hour set today. Rafael is gonna run the dev flow and I will cover the account side and next steps. Samira, Ethan, Marta you all good on audio?
[00:12] Samira Khan: Yep good here, thanks. Slight echo on my side but ok.
[00:18] Rafael Ortiz: Hi all, Rafael here, I'm the SE. I'll do the live steps, try to keep it hands-on.
[00:27] Ethan Brooks: Sounds good. We're most interested in the Python quickstart then porting to TS for our webservice. Also curious about keys and VPC options.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Perfect, that's what we'll hit. Rafael, first step?
[00:40] Rafael Ortiz: Alright, starting with the repo — we shared the quickstart repo link in the calendar notes, but I'll paste in chat again. It's a minimal py and ts example, run with a single env var REDWOOD_API_KEY.
[00:53] Rafael Ortiz: (typing) Ok link's in chat. So clone, pip install -r requirements, there's a sample prompts file. For TS we use npm install and run via node or ts-node.
[01:05] Marta Diaz: Quick question, where should we store the API key for our CI? We use GitHub Actions currently.
[01:12] Rafael Ortiz: Good question — we recommend GitHub secrets or Vault. In the repo we show a .env example but in CI you set REDWOOD_API_KEY as a repo secret and reference it in the workflow step.
[01:22] Samira Khan: And rotation? We have strict rotation policies.
[01:25] Maya Chen: You can create short-lived service tokens via the console and rotate regularly; Rafael will show the token UI later. For SSO we support SAML/Okta to manage admin access; service tokens are separate.
[01:37] Rafael Ortiz: Jumping into the Python demo — running python quickstart.py. (sound of typing) Ok you can see a simple call: client.generate(prompt=...). We show streaming and non-streaming variants.
[01:52] Rafael Ortiz: (demo) Output prints, note we set max_tokens and model=="redwood-1-mini" in the example to keep cost low.
[02:04] Samira Khan: Is the model name exact? We have internal naming conventions and sometimes it confuses ops.
[02:09] Rafael Ortiz: Yeah model names are in the catalog, some are variants — if you need a stable name for CI lock we recommend pinning the versioned model id which we show in the runbook.
[02:21] Ethan Brooks: How does this translate to TypeScript? We have a Node service that needs typed responses.
[02:27] Rafael Ortiz: The TS client mirrors the Python calls. Example: const res = await client.chat.create({messages:[...]}); we include type definitions in the npm package.
[02:36] Rafael Ortiz: We'll also share a small wrapper we use internally to validate structured JSON output using the schema param — that helps with typed parsing on your side.
[02:49] Marta Diaz: You mentioned private deployments earlier — if we wanted the on-prem package what's the onboarding like?
[02:55] Maya Chen: For private we do a prep call, then we provide an image and infra docs. There are two modes: VPC with a private control plane (Redwood manages control plane but you keep network isolation) or fully air-gapped where you run the control plane. Both integrate with KMS and HSM for key management.
[03:12] Samira Khan: Ok do you have SOC2 docs? We need them to move forward.
[03:16] Maya Chen: Yes absolutely, I'll attach SOC2 and ISO docs. Also we'll share a short checklist for compliance and network requirements.
[03:24] Rafael Ortiz: Back to the demo — switching to the console briefly to show how to create a service token. (small pause) Ok in the console here, go to Team -> Service tokens -> Create. You can scope tokens to routes and set TTL.
[03:42] Samira Khan: Can we scope so tokens only access embeddings endpoints? We separate that workload.
[03:47] Rafael Ortiz: Yep you can scope by product surface (embeddings vs generation) and even by model. There is granular RBAC we can connect to your existing IdP.
[03:58] Ethan Brooks: About cost: if we use streaming and batching how does that affect token billing? We want to estimate monthly spend.
[04:06] Maya Chen: Token billing is per input/output token. Batching helps reduce per-request overhead and continuous batching or prefix caching reduces overall tokens sent to the model for repeated prompts. We'll run an estimate with your traffic profile — Rafael can set up a sample calculation.
[04:22] Rafael Ortiz: For an initial estimate send us a few representative prompts and typical concurrency; I'll mock an hourly QPS and token distribution and return some cost buckets.
[04:31] Samira Khan: We'll send a set by Thursday.
[04:34] Maya Chen: Great. Next I'll walk through env patterns for multi-environment. We recommend prefixing env vars REDWOOD_API_KEY_DEV / _STAGE / _PROD. In k8s store these in secrets and reference with projected volumes for pods.
[04:50] Marta Diaz: For our helm charts do you have a recommended snippet?
[04:53] Rafael Ortiz: Yes we have a short helm values example in the repo under infra/helm. It shows a k8s secret with the token and an init container pattern for injecting KV cache.
[05:05] Ethan Brooks: Wait, inject KV cache? We use the model KV cache word — what do you mean by that?
[05:10] Rafael Ortiz: Sorry jargon — KV cache as in the attention key-value cache for generation sessions, not a secret store. We also support prefix caching at the request layer to avoid re-sending large system prompts.
[05:24] Samira Khan: On the topic of security, does Redwood log raw inputs? We need to know about PII retention.
[05:30] Maya Chen: By default we retain inputs for 30 days for debugging but for enterprise customers we can turn off retention and send logs only to your audit endpoint; also support for customer-managed logs. We'll put the settings details in the docs we share.
[05:45] Marta Diaz: Ok good. Another question — any integration example with Datadog for latency tracing?
[05:50] Rafael Ortiz: Yes we have tracing hooks; we emit spans and you can ingest via OTLP. There's also a middleware for Express that captures request-level token counts.
[06:02] Ethan Brooks: Awesome. Can you show a quick failure/fallback? If the dedicated pool is busy what happens?
[06:08] Rafael Ortiz: In the routing policy demo — you can set fallback to a cheaper model or to hosted pool. The client SDK has a retry hook and we recommend an exponential backoff with jitter.
[06:20] Samira Khan: Are there SDK timeouts we should set? We don't want hung calls in our worker pool.
[06:24] Rafael Ortiz: Default is 60s but settable per call; for streaming we keep a heartbeat. We'll add best-practice snippets to the repo.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Ok we're a bit over 60 minutes — quick recap and next steps. Rafael?
[06:40] Rafael Ortiz: Recap: clone quickstart, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env, try python quickstart and ts example, send prompts and traffic, Rafael will run latency/cost estimate.
[06:49] Maya Chen: I'll send SOC2 and VPC docs and create the sandbox creds. Next call we'll scope a short POC for a single endpoint and 2 week pilot. Proposed 2025-09-16 for POC scoping.
[06:58] Ethan Brooks: Works for us.
[07:01] Samira Khan: We'll share prompt set by 2025-09-11.
[07:04] Marta Diaz: Thanks everyone.
[07:06] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links and the action items.

(End of recording)
